messages:
Samir: Quick sync — we need a concise canonical definition for TTFT vs TPOT we can use across replay/synth benches. I'm seeing inconsistent p95 numbers across teams.
Nisha: +1. My take: TTFT = time from request arrival to first token emitted. TPOT = time from request arrival to last token (completion). That maps to user-perceived latency vs end-to-end cost window.
Alex: Agree on definitions. Also add explicit notes about whether we include queueing time from ingress LB or only runtime processing. That changes p95 significantly.
Samir: Good point. Proposal: for our canonical bench, include ingress queue only for replay harnesses (to emulate prod), but exclude it for kernel microbench runs. Keep fields explicit in harness metadata.
Jin: Profiling note — recent kernel swap to opt-v2 increased single-request TTFT by ~8% at 128-token tails under small-batch synthetic. But TPOT improved for long requests due to better attention kernels.
Nisha: Can you paste the perf numbers? We need to see p50/p95/p99 and goodput at QPS points.
Jin: Sure — from last night's run (small-batch, quant32):
```
config: {model: redwood-1b-q32, seq: 128, batch: 1..8, warmup: 500, run: 2000}
results: {TTFT_p50: 48ms, TTFT_p95: 120ms, TTFT_p99: 210ms, TPOT_p95: 420ms, goodput: 85%, QPS_at_SLO: 120}
```
Samir: Nice. Jin — what's the KV cache warmup behavior? Replay harness may benefit from prefix caching, synth not. We should document how we seed KV state.
Jin: For the run above we zeroed KV (cold). I also ran a 'replay-warm' variant (replay trace prefill) — TTFT_p95 dropped to 70ms. So KV prefix caching is huge for interactive traces.
perf-bot: ALERT: regression-detector flagged a 7% TTFT_p95 increase on opt-v2 vs opt-v1 for synth-small-batch. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/alerts/3021 :eyes:
Nisha: Thanks perf-bot. That aligns with Jin's note. We need apples-to-apples: same warmup, same payload distribution, same ingress behavior. Otherwise apples != apples.
Alex: For harness metadata let's add fields: `ingress_included` (bool), `kv_seed` (cold|prefill|trace), `seq_dist` (fixed|empirical), `batch_policy` (static|adaptive), `kernel_variant`. That'll make comparisons sortable.
Samir: Good. Also we should standardize reporting: always include TTFT_p50/p95/p99, TPOT_p50/p95/p99, goodput@SLO, QPS_curve (list).
Jin: I'll attach a small script to convert raw latency samples to those metrics. Also we should capture per-kernel timeline (time spent in attention, matmul, cuda-sync) for regressions.
Nisha: Recommend we add a short checklist for team-run benches: 1) seed KV mode, 2) record ingress, 3) kernel variant locked, 4) reproducible RNG, 5) attach raw samples.
Samir: Action items: Jin to run opt-v1 vs opt-v2 apples-to-apples with both cold and prefill KV by EOD. Alex to update harness schema in repo. Nisha to draft a 1-pager definitions doc for benchmarking guild.
Alex: I'll PR the schema change to `bench/harness/schema.yaml` and add example JSONs.
Jin: Running now. Will ping when upload finishes.
perf-bot: Upload complete: results at https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/88421 (contains raw samples + kernel traces)
Samir: Thanks all. If we see persistent TTFT regressions after kernel tuning, we may need to revisit batching heuristics (adaptive batch thresholds). Flagging @Nisha for prioritization.
Nisha: On it. Will triage after Jin's runs. :thumbsup:
